text:
sarah: @incident-bot paging: P0 - decode p99 spikes observed across prod-gpu pool, multiple customers seeing streaming stalls :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2158. Affected service: runtime-decode. Priority: P0. Paging on-call.

miguel: seeing p95 up ~3x and p99 up ~7x starting ~08:42 UTC. tail latency appears tied to compile/kernels after last deploy (trt8 + new flashattn kernels).

joel: confirmed. dashboards -> runtime-decode -> region=us-west shows sudden stepped increase. stack traces show heavy kernel eviction and retry loops.

alyssa: customers reporting "streaming cutouts" and partial responses. CS flagged 4 high-tier apps. We should assess immediate customer impact and mitigation window.

sarah: quick plan: 1) route new requests away from us-west pool if possible 2) rollback new kernel package on a small canary of nodes 3) enable fallback compile flags to avoid async eviction path. Who can start evicting nodes?

ken: I can kick off routing change. Adding a temporary routing policy: prefer region=us-east for new sessions, scope=hosted-only. Doing now.

ops-bot: Routing update applied: traffic shift ~30% -> us-east. TTL 15m, canary 5%.

miguel: building an emergency hotpatch to revert the compilepath changes (specifically revert -fasync-evict and the new flashattn kernel selection). I'll start a build of kernel-2024.07. Reverting to previous nvcc flags and old trt build. ETA ~14m for artifact.

joel: meanwhile we can reduce batch sizes and force non-flashattn path in model config for streaming customers. Pushing config change to eng-runtime: /prod/models/* -> disable flashattn.

alyssa: notifying account execs for the 4 impacted customers. Preparing a short blurb: "We are investigating increased tail latency impacting streaming, mitigation in progress. Expect partial routing and rollback actions within 30m."

carol: logs from one failing host (gpu-wn-12):
```
E decode: kernel eviction triggered, retry count=3
W compilepath: fallback to generic kernel
I scheduler: ctx-migration 0x7ff failed: -EAGAIN
```
Patterns show hot compilepath allocations causing memory pressure -> trailing stalls.

miguel: build done, uploading artifact to s3://redwood-artifacts/hotpatches/kernel-revert-171902. Starting rolling patch on canary group (2 hosts). I'll watch p99.

sarah: status update when canary patched. If p99 drops, schedule 20% rollout every 5m. If not, abort and try alternative (force no-flashattn + lower batch).

ops-bot: canary patch started: hosts gpu-wn-45, gpu-wn-46. Patch script: `sudo systemctl stop runtime && dpkg -i kernel-revert-171902.deb && systemctl start runtime`

joel: can we instrument per-host p99 alongside kube events? Adding a short loop: `while true; curl metrics | jq '.p99'` per host to stream numbers into thread.

(5m) miguel: canary p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 230ms on gpu-wn-45, gpu-wn-46. No streaming stalls observed in logs post-restart.

sarah: good sign. rolling to 20% now. Ken continue routing to keep some distance for customers until roll reaches 60%.

ken: routing update applied -> us-east preference increased to 60% for new sessions.

alyssa: CS update sent to customers at 09:30 UTC. Asking for any additional errors.

carol: note: while rolling, one host failed healthcheck after patch (gpu-wn-89). Captured logs show crash in trt plugin load. Taking it out of rotation.

miguel: marking host gpu-wn-89 for manual rebuild, skipping auto-rollback. Continuing rollout to remaining canaries.

(20m) joel: overall cluster p95 back to baseline, p99 trending down. One remaining SLO alert for streaming-slo-prod in us-west amplitude 1.12x.

sarah: next steps: 1) complete rollout to 100% in us-west 2) run overnight soak 3) postmortem to include root cause analysis of compilepath regression and release gating gaps (CI didn't catch memory eviction under long-tail streaming)

miguel: filing PR to remove the async-evict flag and add unit + integration tests for long-tail streaming under low-memory scenarios.

alyssa: I'll schedule customer follow-up and include mitigation timeline + what we're changing to prevent recurrence.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-2158 status -> mitigated (rolling revert). Severity P0 -> downgraded to P2 after full rollout observed.

sarah: handing off to night on-call @joel for post-rollout monitoring and postmortem draft. Please include timeline, why TRT/FlashAttn kernel switch bypassed perf tests, and which compiler flags caused eviction regressions.

joel: taking handoff. I'll keep watch and start the postmortem doc. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene tomorrow 11:00 UTC for RCA review.
